title: Temperature-aware KV coalescer + fragmentation hedging for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem: For long-context variants of Llama / Mistral / Qwen we observe suboptimal GPU memory utilization caused by small scattered KV allocations from many concurrent short-lived requests and cold-hotset churn. This increases fragmentation, causes OOMs on heavy tail workloads, and forces conservative batch sizing that hurts throughput.

Proposal: Implement a temperature-aware KV coalescer combined with a splay-based allocator and fragmentation hedging layer. Key concepts:
- Temperature estimation: continuously score KV slabs/entries by "temperature" (access frequency + recency decay + model-variant weight) to separate hot prefix state from cold residuals.
- Coalescer: on allocation path, coalesce small KV writes into pooled slabs when temperature is high to reduce per-allocation overhead and improve locality. For cold writes, use sparse chunking to avoid reserving contiguous GPU memory.
- Splay allocator: adopt a splay-tree-backed free-list that prefers merging nearby free spans and supports fast split/coalesce at ~O(log n) for large-free-span operations to reduce fragmentation.
- Fragmentation hedging: proactive compaction triggers based on occupancy heatmap and predicted incoming sequence-length distribution; use short-time paused compaction across low-priority shards to limit latency spikes.
- Variant-aware packing: maintain per-variant working-set estimates (Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Qwen-14B-long) and bias allocations to pre-reserved pools when serving those variants to reduce cross-variant interference.
- Integration with batching: expose hints to the continuous batcher (max_batch_size override, expected_kv_delta) so the batcher can size micro-batches more aggressively when coalescer reduces fragmentation risk.

Goals: reduce 95th/99th percentile memory occupancy for mixed long/short workloads by 18-30%, decrease OOM rate in stress tests to <0.1% for our 1e6 request/day baseline, and improve throughput by 5-12% for long-context steady-state workloads.

Non-goals: does not change model execution kernels or KV-cache semantic behavior. This is a memory-management and allocation-layer optimization with graceful fallbacks to existing LRU-based eviction and current allocator if safety checks fail.

2026-02-24 - Diego Morales: Ran simulator with 10M synthetic traces (mix 60/30/10 short/medium/long). Baseline fragmentation score 0.43 -> coalescer prototype 0.27. Expected memory drop ~22% for heavy long-context variant mix.
2026-03-02 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Approved scope for Cycle 48. Prioritize safe fallback and observability: add per-alloc telemetry, compaction events, and eviction reasoning tags.
2026-03-05 - Justin Park (SRE): Observability notes: need a high-signal metric for "coalescer-backpressure" and to surface compaction-trigger latency on Console. Created dashboard ticket ENG-742101.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Implementation PR opened. Early internal canary on a dedicated pool (gpu-dedicated-ml-8) shows 11% throughput gain for Mistral long-window workloads and 0.9% p99 latency regression during compaction spikes. Tuned compaction frequency to remove regression.

2026-03-10 - Arielle Chen: Experiment results uploaded. Next steps: extend variant-aware pools to Qwen-14B-long, add safety net to disable coalescer when fragmented free-space ratio < 0.12, and schedule integration tests that replay production KV traces for 72h. Assigned follow-ups to ENG-511200 and ENG-742101.
